text:
Muscle lactate production rises when glycolysis outpaces the mitochondria's ability to oxidize pyruvate, which happens during high-intensity or sustained-maximal exercise, especially with heavy recruitment of fast-twitch fibers. Hypoxia, a high cytosolic NADH/NAD⁺ ratio, and adrenergic stimulation (epinephrine) also push glycolysis, and so lactate, higher. Lactate output falls when exercise intensity drops to levels the oxidative system can match.

CONFIDENCE: 90
